Catalase has the ability to promote the decomposition of hydrogen perox- ide to water and oxygen. It has been applied to wounds and skin ulcers and has also been used in the treatment of eczema. It has sometimes been used with glucose oxidase (p.2313) in food preservation to break down hy- drogen peroxide produced during oxidation of glucose, and is also included in preparations for contact lens care to neutralise hydrogen peroxide. Catalase is a free-radical scavenger and has been investigated for its ability to limit reperfusion injury thought to be related to free- radical production. Combinations of catalase with superoxide dismutase have also been investigated. ◊ References. 1. Greenwald RA. Superoxide dismutase and catalase as therapeu- tic agents for human diseases: a critical review. Free Radic Biol Med 1990; 8: 201–9.
